A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LSRM study. All 21 pages of v1 and 25 pages of v2, including Appendices A–C in v2, support comparison. Text extraction and visual inspection resolve the equations, tables, figures, and relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original LSRM experiments on novel-view synthesis and inverse rendering, including quantitative comparisons, ablations, and reduced-view evaluations in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds resolution ablations, geometry measurements, reconstruction case studies, and a comparison with 3D Gaussian optimization.

M1.justification: The dense-to-sparse residual architecture, geometric block routing, grouped-query attention, and sequence-parallel procedure are retained. v2 presents its expanded loss, normalization, and rendering descriptions as additional implementation details; the PDFs do not establish a revised underlying method.

E1.justification: The 600K training models and GSO, StanfordORB, DigitalTwinCatalogue, and ObjectsWithLighting evaluation coverage are retained. Additional geometry measurements and case studies concern the existing reconstruction tasks. The ten-object GSO subset changes sampling, while reduced-view testing already appears in v1.

E2.justification: Appendix C adds an evaluated 3D Gaussian optimization baseline in Table 7, distinct from the existing feed-forward GS-LRM baseline. Comparator membership in the original Tables 1–4 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds separate image/volume resolution controls at (64,48) and (48,64), DTC normal/depth evaluation, and a ten-object GSO comparison using 16/32/64 views for 3DGS and 8/16 for LSRM. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged; newly specified training settings are disclosures rather than established revisions.

E4.justification: Table 1 extends the existing scaling ablation by varying image and volume resolutions separately. Appendix C and Figure 10 add two case studies examining recovery from inaccurate Stage 1 geometry. These are focused extensions of the existing analyses, rather than a systematic new robustness study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The newly stated random selection of ten GSO objects concerns evaluation sampling, not repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Existing values in Tables 1–4 are retained. New results include ablation PSNRs of 31.68 and 31.82, DTC normal/depth errors of 0.03/0.008, and Table 7's ten-object comparison. Its 34.17 PSNR for 16-view LSRM is subset-specific, not an update to the original 33.08; 64-view 3DGS has better SSIM and LPIPS. v2 also reports approximately five-second sparse-stage inference and 40 GB peak memory.

T1.justification: Appendix B newly defines the complete weighted NVS and inverse-rendering objectives in Equations 16–17, where v1 only summarizes the supervision. Existing reconstruction and attention mathematics is retained after relocation and renumbering. No theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and headline claims: expanded context, geometric routing, balanced sequence parallelism, and improved reconstruction fidelity. The reported token-scaling factors and headline PSNR/LPIPS gains are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the separate ablations as showing a larger contribution from volume-token scaling and explains how selecting nearby voxels permits recovery from coarse geometric errors. It also expands the inverse-rendering ambiguity discussion to albedo, roughness, and metallicity shifts. Existing material-estimation and tiny-text limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands reproducibility information with AdamW settings, normalization, FSDP, stage-wise iterations, learning rates, batch/crop sizes, selected-block counts, explicit loss weights, deferred rendering, and material color space. It additionally specifies camera sampling and inference resources. The abstract changes the code-and-weights statement from a planned release to reported availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds five references covering QK normalization, AdamW, the PyTorch NSA implementation, deferred rendering, and LPIPS; existing cited works remain. Related work additionally distinguishes single-view generative appearance synthesis from posed multi-view reconstruction and describes the settings as complementary.

P1.justification: The NSA background moves from Section 3.1 to Appendix A, accompanied by subsection renumbering and a supplementary-material structure. Local wording, terminology, and cross-reference corrections improve the text, while the main narrative remains largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 expands Table 1, adds Tables 5–7 and Figure 10, and reformats several existing table headers and captions. Existing Figures 1–9 retain their visual content, with relocations as the document reflows. Figure 1's stated input range changes from 12–18 to 6–18 views.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility by supplying training specifications and explicit objectives missing from v1, and strengthens supporting evidence through separate scaling ablations and geometry comparisons. The original results remain intact. The new robustness evidence consists of illustrative cases, and the 3DGS comparison covers only ten objects, making the overall improvement useful but limited.
